primitives.name: Official Assignment Shadow
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### Officials / Referees Use only licensed assignment and historical same-sport trend feeds.
primitives.assumptions: Licensed data integrity, ergodicity of assignment patterns.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Small sample sizes, playoff season, rare crew compositions.

layer2.mapping: Conforms to GSE's situational reasoning via referee bias matrices.
layer2.telemetry: Historical win-rate differentials by assigned official crews.

primitives.name: Venue Environment State
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### Venue Environment Use venue coordinates plus game-time weather/roof/surface state.
primitives.assumptions: Spatial homogeneity, temporal stationarity of environmental effects.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Extreme weather anomalies, stadium renovations, daylight saving transitions.

layer2.mapping: Integrates into GSE's state-transition logic for environmental covariates.

primitives.name: Evidence Readiness Matrix
primitives.verbatim_quote: Evidence Readiness Matrix decides whether each factor is ACTIVE, SHADOW_READY, SHADOW_COLLECTING, BLOCKED, or ABSENT.
primitives.assumptions: Discrete event classification, monotonic information flow.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Transition points between readiness states, threshold crossings.

layer2.mapping: Serves as a control variable in GSI's scoring algorithms for active factors.

primitives.name: Weather Signal Decay
primitives.verbatim_quote: decisions - wind shifts near first pitch/kickoff - incorrectly geocoded stadiums Matrix posture: - weather can be useful quickly, but it must age out aggressively.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t': 'time in minutes since event start', 'w(t)': 'weather influence factor (dimensionless)', 'τ': 'decay time constant (minutes)'}
primitives.assumptions: Weather impact decays exponentially with time; initial influence is deterministic but diminishes rapidly.

layer2.mapping: Weather signal strength is modeled as an exponential decay kernel applied to temporal proximity of game start.
layer2.telemetry: Observed deviation from expected outcome due to weather misalignment

primitives.name: Pace-Based Team Rate Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### Pace / Team Rates Use league/team stat feeds, not LLM summaries.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'r_i(t)': "team i's rate of action at time t (actions/minute)", 'S_i': "team i's statistical baseline (actions/minute)"}
primitives.assumptions: League/team statistics provide stable, unbiased estimates of team behavior patterns.
primitives.breakdown_regime: r_i(t) ≈ S_i when t is within normal season range

layer2.mapping: Pace rates are mapped to stochastic process intensity functions in GSE's temporal state space.
layer2.telemetry: Deviation between predicted and actual action frequency during game

primitives.name: Shadow Source Validation Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: Candidate source class: - SportsDataIO, Sportradar, or league APIs where legally allowed Risks: - early-season samples - injuries changing tempo - garbage-time distortion Matrix posture: - SHADOW_ONLY until bucket-level Brier improvement is measured.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B(t)': 'Brier score at time t (unitless)', 'β': 'validation threshold (unitless)', 'S_{sh}(t)': 'shadow source reliability indicator (0 to 1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Early data is unreliable; validation occurs only after sufficient sample size and performance metrics.

layer2.mapping: Source validation uses Brier score thresholds to gate real-time integration into prediction models.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy gain in model calibration post-validation

primitives.name: Aggressive Safety Boundary
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is the layer that lets the product become aggressive later without becoming sloppy now.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A(t)': 'aggressiveness level at time t (unitless)', 'S(t)': 'safety constraint at time t (unitless)', 'T': 'transition time point (time units)'}
primitives.assumptions: Safety constraints must be maintained while allowing strategic aggression to emerge over time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: t ≤ T ⇒ A(t) ≤ S(t); t > T ⇒ A(t) ≥ S(t)

layer2.mapping: The boundary enforces a control-theoretic constraint on policy exploration vs exploitation trade-offs.
layer2.telemetry: Change in decision variance before and after transition time

The core idea revolves around temporal dynamics of data utility—specifically, how weather signals degrade over time, necessitating rapid aging-out mechanisms. This aligns with Bayesian updating where prior beliefs are adjusted based on new evidence, but also requires explicit handling of signal decay. The emphasis on using league/team stat feeds rather than LLM summaries reflects a preference for empirically grounded data over speculative inference, which is critical for maintaining model integrity. The shadow validation protocol ensures that only validated sources contribute to real-time predictions, mitigating risk from noisy or biased inputs.
